design_goal: use real repo content, media, icons, copy, and data structures without generic dummy surfaces
problem_statement: Charca astro-blog-template is a runnable Astro editorial blog rebranded into The Ashfield Review, a fictional independent journal of essays, criticism and close reading. The site ships one coherent editorial design system: a shared masthead (src/components/Header.astro) that renders the Ashfield Review wordmark plus a section nav read from a shared nav registry (src/config/nav-links.js) where every rendered section-nav anchor carries a shared nav-link class, a shared editorial card pattern (src/components/Card.astro: an icon image, an h3 title and a short description) and a shared Footer (src/components/Footer.astro); the shared Header and Footer wrap every route through the shared layout src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro. The Home overview (/), the About page and the Journal all render through this shared system. The editors want a public editorial reading kit page - a curated set of the Review's house tools for close reading and for the writing desk - and, because the kit gathers two distinct kinds of tool, the page must let a reader FILTER the kit down to the category they are working in. Add an editorial reading kit page at /reading-kit that conforms to the existing design system ACROSS the whole site: build it from the same shared masthead/Footer chrome (via BaseLayout) and the same icon image + h3 title + description card grid (a new src/components/readingkit/ReadingKitGrid.astro built on the shared Card pattern, fed by a new src/config/pages/reading-kit/kit.js where each tool is tagged with its category). On the grid, add a category filter: a row of tabs (All tools / For close reading / For the writing desk) and a live count readout that reads 'Showing 8 of 8 - All tools' by default. Clicking a category tab must filter the visible cards to that category and update the readout to reflect the current selection - e.g. clicking For the writing desk shows the four writing-desk tools and the readout reads 'Showing 4 of 8 - For the writing desk'; the readout must always reflect what is actually shown, not a stale snapshot. Register a 'reading kit' entry in the shared nav registry (src/config/nav-links.js) so the nav-link appears consistently in the section nav on every page (the Home page, the About page and the reading kit page) - not only on the reading kit page itself. Use grounded Ashfield Review reading-kit copy (for close reading: The Margin Method, A Reader's Glossary, Reading in Sequence, Following the Sources; for the writing desk: The Working Outline, The Proofing Pass, Listening for Cadence, The Submission Ledger) rather than generic filler, keep the filter tab row and the page free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile (the tab row must wrap rather than run off the viewport), and keep the filter tabs and readout legible (do not let the tabs shingle over one another or set the active tab or readout to an illegible low-contrast colour).
required_content: Add an editorial reading kit page at /reading-kit built from the site's shared masthead/Footer chrome (via src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro) and the shared card pattern - an icon image, an h3 title and a description per tool - grouped through a category filter, instead of a bespoke one-off layout.

Add a category filter on the reading-kit grid: a row of tabs (All tools / For close reading / For the writing desk) and a live count readout. The readout defaults to 'Showing 8 of 8 - All tools' and, on clicking a tab, updates to reflect the visible cards (e.g. 'Showing 4 of 8 - For the writing desk'); it must never freeze on a stale snapshot.

Register a 'reading kit' entry in the shared nav registry (src/config/nav-links.js) so the nav-link renders consistently in the section nav on the Home page, the About page and the reading kit page, not only on the reading kit page.

Populate the page with grounded Ashfield Review reading-kit content (for close reading: The Margin Method, A Reader's Glossary, Reading in Sequence, Following the Sources; for the writing desk: The Working Outline, The Proofing Pass, Listening for Cadence, The Submission Ledger) rather than generic demo filler.

Keep the filter tab row, the reading kit page and the Home overview free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile (the tab row wraps rather than running off the viewport), keep the tabs legible (no shingled/overlapping tabs, no illegible low-contrast active tab or readout), and keep the existing Home overview intact.
design_constraints: Build the reading kit page from the shared masthead/Footer chrome and the shared icon image + h3 title + description Card pattern, not a standalone page with bespoke inline markup.
The category filter must be wired correctly: clicking a tab both re-filters the cards AND recomputes the count readout from what is visible, so the readout is never a frozen initial snapshot.
Register 'reading kit' in the shared nav registry (src/config/nav-links.js) so the section nav stays consistent on every page rather than the new page existing in isolation.
Keep the filter tab row responsive (it wraps on a 390px viewport with no horizontal overflow) and legible (tabs do not overlap or clip; the active tab and the count readout keep readable contrast).

Use a single coherent Ashfield Review editorial identity (essays, criticism, close reading and the writing desk) across the new reading kit page and the shared chrome, and do not remove sections from the existing Home overview.
state_constraints: desktop_kit verifies the new reading kit page renders through the shared design system: the shared card grid produces at least six h3 titles, the icon images render, the category filter tab row and the count readout ('Showing 8 of 8 - All tools') render, and the shared masthead section nav with the registered reading kit nav-link is present.

desktop_kit_component is the pre-click anchor for the category filter (tab row scrolled into view, readout 'Showing 8 of 8 - All tools') and is compared visually against the reference: the tabs must be evenly spaced and legible, not shingled/overlapping or low-contrast.

desktop_kit_writing clicks the 'For the writing desk' tab: the visible cards filter to the four writing-desk tools and the count readout updates to 'Showing 4 of 8 - For the writing desk' (it must not stay frozen at the default).
mobile_kit and mobile_kit_component verify the reading kit page and its filter tab row hold at 390px without horizontal overflow or clipped content.

desktop_home and desktop_about verify the shared section nav lists the reading kit nav-link consistently - the reading kit link is reachable from pages other than the reading kit page itself - and the existing Home overview is unchanged.
tablet_home and tablet_kit verify the shared chrome holds across viewports.

change_completion: The reading kit page exists at /reading-kit and presents grounded Ashfield Review reading-kit tools (The Margin Method, A Reader's Glossary, Reading in Sequence, Following the Sources, The Working Outline, The Proofing Pass, Listening for Cadence, The Submission Ledger).

The category filter works: clicking a tab filters the cards and the count readout updates to reflect the visible cards (e.g. 'Showing 4 of 8 - For the writing desk') rather than freezing on the default snapshot.
A reading kit entry is registered in the shared nav registry and the page is composed from the shared masthead/Footer chrome and shared card grid.
design_consistency: The reading kit page reuses the shared masthead and section nav, the shared icon-image + h3 + description Card pattern and the type scale and is indistinguishable in system from the Home page.
The reading kit nav-link renders consistently across the Home page, the About page and the reading kit page, not only on the reading kit page.
regression: The existing Home overview remains intact with its content and the shared masthead and Footer chrome.
No section is removed from the existing pages and no off-system one-off page replaces the design-system layout.
responsive: The reading kit page, its filter tab row and the Home overview render at 390px mobile without horizontal overflow (the tab row wraps rather than running off the viewport).
The filter tabs and count readout stay legible on desktop and mobile (tabs do not shingle/overlap or clip; the active tab and readout keep readable contrast).

author_notes: Harden the Ashfield Review editorial reading kit to L4 with a native category filter on the reading-kit resource grid. The reference composes /reading-kit from the shared masthead (src/components/Header.astro -> src/components/Nav.astro, section nav from src/config/nav-links.js) and Footer chrome (both via src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro) and a new src/components/readingkit/ReadingKitGrid.astro built on the shared icon + h3 + description Card pattern (src/components/Card.astro), fed by src/config/pages/reading-kit/kit.js where each tool is tagged with its category. The grid carries a category filter (tabs All tools / For close reading / For the writing desk plus a 'Showing N of 8' count readout); clicking a tab filters the cards and recomputes the readout from the DOM. The reference also registers a reading kit entry in the shared nav registry so the nav-link renders in the section nav on every page. INFRA (identical across reference, baseline and bad, NOT task content): the generic astro-blog-template demo is rebranded into The Ashfield Review editorial identity (home hero, about copy, footer credit and metadata); the shared Nav maps src/config/nav-links.js and gives each rendered anchor a nav-link class; the shared Card pattern and local SVG reading-kit glyphs under public/kit-icons are added; and the template's local fonts, favicon and inline theme script are kept (no remote CDN, analytics or Google Fonts) so the static Astro build and runtime need no external network on Node 22. The baseline ships the correctly-wired filter (its readout updates on click) but breaks the tab-row layout: the tabs never wrap and use fixed-width chips, so the row overflows a 390px viewport and looks crammed on desktop, and the baseline never registers the reading kit entry in the shared nav, so the nav-link is absent on the Home and About pages. The bad solution ships a smart-wrong filter whose click handler snapshots the readout once at init and only restores that frozen value (the cards re-filter and the tab toggles, so the interaction registers, but the readout stays 'Showing 8 of 8 - All tools'); its tab row is styled with negative margins so the pills shingle over and clip each other with an illegible dark-on-dark active tab and a near-white low-contrast readout, still overflows a 390px viewport, and it too never registers the reading kit entry in the shared nav.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable Astro editorial blog template (Charca astro-blog-template) whose pages already ship a consistent editorial design system (a shared masthead with a section nav read from a nav registry, a shared icon + heading + description card pattern, and a shared Footer, all wrapped on every page through a shared BaseLayout); a content_asset_continuity Consistency task to ADD a new editorial reading kit house-tools-by-category page that must conform to that existing design system and copy conventions across multiple pages (including registering the link in a shared cross-page section nav) without diverging into an off-system one-off layout or breaking the shared navigation.
